# Independent PEA fixtures

These 19 archives were generated by the `pea` executable bundled with
[PeaZip portable 11.4.0, Linux GTK2 x86-64](https://github.com/peazip/PeaZip/releases/tag/11.4.0).
The extracted package directory is `peazip_portable-11.4.0.LINUX.GTK2.x86_64`.
Generator executable SHA-256:
`4a0ec582fbded8f4bffc5d95c5e33e28bda9d1b3dc97831767cbdae39e21010a`.
The archives contain only input created for these tests; no third-party user data
or executable generator is included. `SHA256SUMS` records the exact checked-in bytes.

The ordinary input tree contains `source/`, `source/empty-dir/`,
`source/empty.bin`, and `source/中文 Ω.txt`. The last file contains
`b"PEA independently generated block\n" * 4000 + bytes(range(256))` (136256 bytes),
SHA-256 `6050ccb8eb47ba3d20954ffe26ed6a5d1c812518115a7a682bbbba08bc70ec6e`.
The separately generated multiblock input is `b"A" * 1048576 + bytes(range(17))`,
SHA-256 `c29c45cb10645a27d37ba63e00e7f2f1c1e5e860d8a28753dff84d68cf4ef341`.

A generation command is:

```sh
pea PEA /tmp/output 0 PCOMPRESS2 CRC32 CRC32 CRC32 HIDDEN FROMCL /tmp/source
```

The three checksum arguments select object, stream and volume hashes. The fourteen
`*-pcompress2.pea` cases use NOALGO, ADLER32, CRC32, CRC64, MD5, RIPEMD160, SHA1,
SHA256, SHA512, WHIRLPOOL, SHA3_256, SHA3_512, BLAKE2S or BLAKE2B at all three layers.
`crc32-pcompress0.pea` uses Store; `level1.pea` and `level3.pea` use PCOMPRESS1/3.
`mixed.pea` uses different checksums at the three layers. `multiblock.pea` contains
more than one 1 MiB block and an incompressible final block stored verbatim.
The native producer records absolute input paths and filesystem timestamps;
regeneration elsewhere can change archive hashes while preserving extracted bytes.

Tests compare extracted bytes with the original input SHA-256, rather than with
another GeeZipX-generated archive. Negative cases are derived in memory: proper
prefix truncations, trailing bytes, invalid headers and algorithms, encrypted
flags, checksum corruption, wrong zlib lengths/trailers, unsafe paths, duplicates,
file ancestors, symlinks, metadata budgets, short/interrupted reads, cancellation,
source changes, failed writes and preservation of an existing destination.

The implementation follows the public-domain
[PEA format specification](https://peazip.github.io/pea-file-format.html).
This corpus covers a single unencrypted stream/volume with UTF-8/ASCII names.
It does not establish compatibility with encryption/HMAC, split volumes,
legacy ANSI code pages, ECC, or every historical PEA variant.
